lens: story & curiosity: arc, stakes, emotion, pacing, memorable images, plants and payoffs
summary: A real step up. Almost every round-1 story note landed in the script and the narration. L1104 now reads 'It sounded sensible, at the time.' L1516b answers the second question aloud. Rosenblatt's 'Love. Hope. Despair.' is voiced, Hopfield's 'nobody remembered the talk' seeds his Nobel, L0616 voices the fog plant, and L0832 pays it off over the bowl, the BY HAND stencil and the foggy hills. Kelcey's 'biggest incorrect prediction' gives the Transformer dive a human turn, and ch12 now flows from the door to Rosenblatt's 1961 note into the stampede. The plant ledger is now complete to the ear: case file to first note, the 1961 note to 'language was the door', the waiting note to scaling laws, 'Who paid for dinner?', 'Remember him' to Widrow's death, the edge of the light to 'Now, it found him', and Hinton's own slip off the Wall. Four things hold story at 8. (1) The film's last spoken image, 'Somewhere tonight a lamp is on...', still plays over near-black (ch15-s09, 34:58-35:05). The match strikes only after the line ends, which was a round-1 fix and is not applied. (2) Act 3, from about 29:10 to 33:30, is still a docket of position tags and news props with no planted question. ch14 never voices the question it answers. (3) ch12-s03 still spends about 22 s of a 36 s shot on one lab's founding, self-description and funding ledger. Bard, LLaMA and GPT-4 get 5 s at the end, so the stampede deflates into accounting. (4) A new orphan: L1416 'But America employed the most.' is the only spoken line in ch14-s05, and its contrast (China's 47%) is on a card only, so the ear hears 'But... the most' with no subject. Fix these four and story and curiosity both reach about 9.
previousRoundCheck: Round-1 story issues. FIXED in script and audio: L1104, L1517 (now 'goes to Hinton, back in 2017'), L1516b, the ch12 reorder and L1206 rewrite, L0312, L0109 prologue pacing (now 187-195 wpm, down from 229-264, not quite the 150 target), L1410 split, L1522 split with L1524 moved to a card, L0616, L1007, L0524b. FIXED in picture: ch08-s13b (the bowl, BY HAND and fog cut is in, and the tall man appears at the desk, though only as 'him' ends at 37.2 s), ch01-s05 (ghost candles of different lengths now read at 54-56 s), ch03-s06 (the quote card lands on the spoken words). NOT FIXED: ch15-s09 (6 s of near-black under L1520, re-raised as major). ch14-s04b/ch14 (no voiced question for Act 3; the docket remains). The global lab-balance note on the ch15-s08 dark lantern (still only the Anthropic card). ch15-s10 (the SOURCES card still renders 'published with the film', and the blank card frames between cards remain, although script.json now holds the URL, so the shot was never re-fit).

issues.problem: This was a round-1 fix and it is still unapplied. L1520 'Somewhere tonight a lamp is on, and someone at the rim is suspicious. That is where new candles come from.' runs from 15.14 to 22.33 s. The frames from +16.5 to +22.1 are nearly black, with only a faint window and a speck of cursor. The match flares at +22.38, after the last word. The film's final spoken image says 'a lamp is on' while the picture shows nothing, and the ending loses its warmth.
issues.fix: From +15.1, keep a small desk lamp or monitor glow clearly lit (at least 25% luminance in its pool) with the cursor steady, so 'a lamp is on' (about +16.6) shows a lamp. Bring the hand and matchbox in on 'suspicious' (about +18.6), strike on 'new' (about +21.2) and catch the wick on 'candles' (about +21.6). Settle the flame on 'come from', then hold the lit candle 2 s before the fade.

issues.problem: 'But America employed the most.' is the only spoken line in ch14-s05. Its contrast, China's 47% of top NeurIPS authors by first degree, appears only on the card, so to the ear 'But' and 'the most' have no referent. It plays right after 'China trailing by years? That belief burned about two.', so a listener may even hear it as 'America employed the most chips'.
issues.fix: Voice both halves (e13-talent): 'Many of the field's top researchers first studied in China. But America employed the most of them.' Re-narrate L1416 alone at about 0.9 speed. ch14-s05 has about 4 s of silent tail to absorb it; re-fit the 'studied' beat to the first sentence and 'work' to 'employed'.

issues.problem: Act 3 pacing, about 29:13 to 33:30, is still a docket. Chips, the DeepSeek receipt, o1, the market fall, position tags, talent, Bletchley, the hotline, the gap tags, the Pentagon case, a settlement card and a warning shot pass in four minutes. There is no question the viewer is waiting to see answered; the round-1 suggestion of a voiced question was not adopted. Every earlier act has a plant ('If one exists', 'Who paid for dinner?', 'why choose the fog?'), so this stretch is where curiosity drops, right before the finale.
issues.fix: Plant one voiced question at the chokepoint candle and pay it off. Extend L1405: '...and China is one to three years behind. Put that in the file: does a fence around chips hold?' Then L1418 answers it: 'The fence still stands, argued over. As of October 2026, nobody agrees how wide the gap is, or whether it will close.' Re-narrate L1405 and L1418, and re-fit ch14-s02 (2.5 s longer) and ch14-s07.

issues.problem: ch12-s03 runs 36 s. About 22 s go to one lab: its founding, its self-description, and a ledger written row by row (FTX, Amazon, Google). Then Bard, LLaMA, GPT-4 and Claude are packed into the last 5 s. Narratively the 'stampede' (L1219) deflates into accounting. Under the brief's no-promotion rule, Anthropic remains the only runner given a founding story, a motto and a funding history inside the race. OpenAI got its founding in ch09; Google, Meta and DeepSeek get none of this.
issues.fix: Cut L1208 to an on-screen ledger card only, with the FTX caveat kept in the card text. Keep L1206 and L1207. Rebalance the shot so the runners race: after L1207, spend the freed about 9 s on the four chips (Bard, LLaMA, GPT-4, Claude) landing one per beat, with the same-day pair struck together. Re-fit ch12-s03 and the m16 cue so the stampede energy carries through to the end of the shot.

issues.problem: Re-raised from round 1 and still unapplied. The unresolved mystery that closes the film, 'one lantern is still dark', is shown only with an Anthropic quote card ('about a quarter of the prompts... Anthropic, 2025'). It comes right after the Anthropic rhyme study (L1504), so the closing question reads as framed by one lab, and the credits then name Anthropic again.
issues.fix: On 'how, exactly, it reaches its answers' (b10), add an independent card beside the Anthropic one, for example Jain & Wallace 2019, 'Attention is not Explanation' [e10-attention-explanation], or another academic interpretability source from the bible. Label the pair 'the field, 2019-2025', so the dark lantern belongs to everyone.

issues.problem: The end cards were not re-fit. The SOURCES card still renders 'published with the film', although script.json now carries 'SOURCES · orly.brett-lamy.workers.dev/generated/neural-net-history/sources'. Each card still crossfades through an empty card-stock frame (+0.5 s, +11.3 s, +23.5 s). Thirty-one seconds of cards after the match is a long, flat exit for an ending that should linger on the new candle.
issues.fix: Re-render from the current script: show the real sources URL, crossfade text to text with no blank stock, and drop the first grey frame. Trim the card section to about 22 s, or keep the lit candle from ch15-s09 faintly behind the parchment so the last image stays the new flame.

issues.problem: On 'Love' (+9.5) the Rosenblatt puppet throws both arms straight up, like a cheer, and holds the pose through 'Hope'. The line is meant to be read lower, without a smile, as the emotional plant for his drowning at L0409. The gesture plays it as triumph and undercuts the most human beat Act 1 has.
issues.fix: Replace the arms-up pose with a stilled one. On 'Love' he lowers his hands and turns his head toward the window; on 'Hope' a hand rests on the sill; on 'Despair' his head dips slightly and he stays still until the slip. Keep the earlier cheerful 'none whatever' gestures, so the contrast does the work.

issues.problem: L0821 'A bad back kept Hinton from flying. Yann LeCun stood at the rear of a packed room.' is read at 224 wpm, the only line over 200 (pacing QA FAIL). It is the hush before the film's climax, Florence, and the human detail (Hinton absent, his old rival watching from the back) rushes past just as it should build tension.
issues.fix: Re-narrate L0821 alone at speed about 0.85, with breath punctuation in spoken: 'A bad back kept Hinton from flying. ... Yann LeCun stood at the rear of a packed room.' Aim for about 150 wpm. ch08-s11 has about 2 s of tail to absorb it.

issues.problem: 'The last word goes to Hinton, back in 2017.' now works, but it drops the film's longest epithet thread, the man 'near the edge of the light' (L0416, L0832b). The farewell to the quiet protagonist could rhyme with that thread, and it does not.
issues.fix: 'The last word goes to the man from the edge of the light, back in 2017.' Re-narrate L1517 only. The on-screen 'HINTON · SEPT 2017' card keeps the name clear.

issues.problem: This is still a 39 s shot of iconographic props: seals, a drone, a courthouse, a book stack, a glass bell and a building. The '$1.5B SETTLEMENT · PIRATED BOOKS' card appears in silence with no lab named, so it reads as an unexplained news item in the middle of 'the labs, under the same light'.
issues.fix: Either name the party on the card ('Anthropic · authors' class action · $1.5B settlement · approved July 2026'), or drop the card and spend those 4 s on a slow push into the row of lamps under 'the same light'. Give the shot one through-line image, every lab's lamp on one shelf, and light each lamp on its own sentence.

best_moments: ch01-s04 / L0109: the lamp clicks on, the WHO TAUGHT IT? card is pinned, and OpenAI's own admission is filed. Twenty seconds in, the case-file frame is set and the viewer is hooked.
ch02-s04 / L0209: 'Each belief gets one, burning as long as it was held.' One rule turns 80 years into a bar chart in wax.
ch03-s06 / L0312: 'At the moment, none whatever,' said cheerfully, then 'Love. Hope. Despair.' Now voiced, it makes Rosenblatt's drowning two minutes later land as a loss.
ch05-s01 / L0524b: 'I have never met anyone who remembered hearing the talk.' A wry seed that pays off 24 minutes later with a 2 a.m. Nobel phone call.
ch06-s05 to ch07-s01: 'So who paid for dinner? Keep that question.' ... 'Both men. Each man lost one bet.' A complete plant and payoff with real wit.

ch06-s08 to ch08-s13b: the voiced 'why would anyone choose the fog?' is paid off over the clean bowl stamped BY HAND, then the foggy hills: 'the net cut its own, many layers deep: deep learning.' This is now the film's thesis, felt.
ch08-s04: the pierced tin stencil over a stitched 4, its sum to 3.88, then 'slide the same stencil everywhere. A convolution.'
ch08-s12 / L0823: the error drops 10.9 points and the narrator says only 'A cliff.'
ch08-s13b / L0832b: 'Thirty-six years near the edge of the light. Now, it found him.' The lamp pool reaches the tall man at the desk.
ch10-s06 and s07: the jug of light pouring softmax into cups, then divide-by-eight as 'learning freezes' against 'pours softly'.
ch12-s06 to s07: 'Not a new engine. A new door.' The first case-file note returns, then Rosenblatt's 1961 card: 'sixty-one years on: language was the door.'
ch13-s01: Hinton physically takes his own '30 TO 50 YEARS' slip off the Wall, a slip planted in the first minute, and the file reopens on a spoken second question.

ch15-s08 / L1514 and L1516b: 'The board was a network all along.' The case board rewires into lanterns, one still dark, and 'how far, how fast? That file stays open.' Both of the film's questions are closed or held open aloud.
